text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Business property leasing in Helsinki has become the liveliest in years and only 2.3 percent of real estate in the city centre was vacant last autumn, Statistics Finland says.
- Families with many children to be taken by surprise by higher daycare fees in August.
- First women in tests to become fighter pilots -- 13 of 225 in final testing are female.
- Leftist Alliance party secretary Ralf Sund accuses the party's anti-EMU wing of using the EMU argument for attempts to alter the party policy.
- Last week's U.S.-Russia summit brought about six million markka of revenue to Finnish businesses but costs for arrangers excluding security rose to about 7.5 million, estimates show.
- Building materials wholesaler Starckjohann's debt restructuring has been a good deal for SKOPBank and Merita which took control of the troubled group in 1994.
- The average lease for business property in Helsinki has returned to European levels at 116.40 markka per square metre, European Property Bulletin says.
- Banks want the government to integrate its financial supervision which monitors banks with its watchdog over insurers.

- Finnish companies last year fought against falling prices by increasing efficiency but an increase in sales did not boost resuts or operating margins, a study of 80 companies with net sales over 100 million markka shows.
- Property investment company Realinvest -- owned by Merita, SOK and OKOBANK -- plans to invest tens of millions of markka in new construction in Helsinki centre.
- Finland hurriedly passing new firearms laws to avoid a case against EU for violating its firearms directives.
- Mustard oil can safely be used as fuel in diesel engines, tests show.
- The risk of food poisoning epidemics are rising due to falling standards in food inspection.
